headline: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport killed 3 Saudi nationals, officials say

Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said on Friday that three Saudi nationals were killed and several people were injured in two ⁠attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday.
In a statement on X, the General Authority of Civil Aviation said the first attack targeted airport facilities, while ⁠the second struck an aircraft ​belonging ⁠to Saudi state carrier Saudia.
The injuries ranged from minor to severe, and the attacks caused material ⁠damage, it said, adding that airport operations had resumed ​and ⁠air traffic had returned ‌to normal.
The aftermath of an explosion at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday.via ReutersYemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Thursday they had attacked the airport with two cruise missiles.
The ‌group also said it had targeted ‌an airport in the southwestern city of Najran, a claim Saudi authorities have not confirmed, and an airbase in Khamis Mushait ⁠with ballistic missiles.
The Houthis say they are targeting the kingdom over its support for government forces in Yemen’s reignited civil war. Saudi Arabia says it is backing an offensive by Yemen’s U.N.-recognized government to take back territory from the Houthis.
